selection.q: What material do jaw plates use?
selection.a: Most fixed and movable jaw plates are cast in high-manganese steel (Mn13, Mn18 and variants) for work-hardening under impact. We can also review alloy options for your specific feed and abrasion conditions.

selection.q: Can you produce to my drawing or part number?
selection.a: Yes. Send the drawing, 3D model, part number or a sample, and the review confirms geometry, material grade, hardness and inspection requirements before quoting.

selection.q: Which crusher brands do you cover?
selection.a: We produce to reference across major jaw crusher models. If the exact reference is not listed, send the part number or sample and we will match it.

selection.q: How do I choose a jaw crusher jaw plate?
selection.a: Start with the crusher model, fixed or movable position, feed rock, feed size, closed-side setting and the current wear pattern. Those details help us review the jaw plate profile and choose Mn13, Mn18 or an alloy option before quoting.

title: Cone Crusher Wear Parts | Mantles & Concaves | DINGDAR
cardDesc: Mantle liners, concave and bowl liners, and upper housing castings for cone crushers in mining and aggregate circuits.
intro: Mantle liners, concave and bowl liners, gyratory concaves and upper housing castings for cone crushers — cast in manganese and alloy grades, produced to your model reference, drawing or sample. For cone crusher liner analysis, we compare the mantle and concave geometry with your chamber profile, feed conditions and wear pattern before quoting.
specs: Material: High-manganese steel for mantles & concaves; alloy grades reviewed per chamber profile
Casting routes: Green sand / shell moulding / lost foam, matched to liner geometry
Machining: As-cast or machined surfaces to drawing, as agreed in review
Inspection: Material, dimensional, hardness and visual records per order; third-party on request
MOQ & lead time: Confirmed during technical review

selection.q: What is the difference between mantle and concave?
selection.a: The mantle is the moving crushing member and the concave (or bowl liner) is the fixed member of the crushing chamber. Both are wear parts replaced together as the chamber profile controls product shape and throughput.

selection.q: Which grades do you cast for cone parts?
selection.a: High-manganese steel for mantles and concaves, and alloy grades where a specific chamber profile or application requires it. Material is confirmed against your working conditions during review.

selection.q: Can you match a specific chamber profile?
selection.a: Yes — send the part number, drawing or a worn sample, and we produce to the original chamber geometry with the agreed crushing profile.

selection.q: How do you analyze cone crusher liners before quoting?
selection.a: We review the mantle or concave reference, crusher model, chamber profile, feed material, feed size, closed-side setting and current wear pattern. Those details help confirm the liner geometry, manganese or alloy grade, inspection scope and quotation basis.

title: Impact Crusher Wear Parts | Blow Bars | DINGDAR
cardDesc: Blow bars, impact plates and liners for impact crushers, cast in high-chromium, alloy and manganese grades.
intro: Blow bars, impact plates and further impact crusher wear references, produced by casting in high-chromium, alloy and manganese grades to your model, drawing or sample.
specs: Material: High-chromium cast iron (Cr15–Cr26), alloy and manganese grades, matched to feed conditions
Casting routes: Green sand / shell moulding / lost foam, matched to bar profile and size
Machining: Keyways and fixing geometry machined to original profile
Inspection: Material, dimensional, hardness and visual records per order; third-party on request
MOQ & lead time: Confirmed during technical review

selection.q: When is high-chromium cast iron the right choice for blow bars?
selection.a: High-chromium cast iron suits abrasive feed with controlled impact. Where feed contains larger, harder rocks, alloy or manganese grades with higher toughness may be preferred. The review matches grade to your working conditions.

selection.q: Do you produce blow bars to original profiles?
selection.a: Yes — original profile, keyway and fixing geometry are reproduced from the part number, drawing or sample, and confirmed before production.

selection.q: What should we send for an impact crusher wear parts quotation?
selection.a: Send the crusher make and model, part number or drawing, a clear photo or sample if available, the feed material and typical feed size, the required quantity and the delivery country. These details let the technical review confirm the profile, material, inspection scope and quotation basis.

selection.q: Can inspection records ship with impact crusher wear parts?
selection.a: Material certificates, dimensional inspection reports, hardness records and visual inspection records can be supplied as agreed. NDT or third-party inspection can also be arranged when specified before production.

selection.q: How are MOQ and lead time confirmed for blow bars?
selection.a: MOQ and lead time depend on the bar geometry, pattern or tooling status, material, heat treatment, machining, inspection scope and quantity. They are confirmed during the technical review rather than guessed before the part reference is known.

selection.q: Which inspection records should accompany an impact crusher wear parts order?
selection.a: The agreed package can include material certificates, dimensional inspection reports, hardness records and visual inspection records. NDT or third-party inspection can be added when the requirement is specified before production.
